name: Bilateral Frontal Polymicrogyria

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Neuroimaging and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Polymicrogyria

criteria.description: MRI evidence of polymicrogyria predominantly affecting bilateral frontal lobes
Presence of early-onset focal or generalized seizures
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability
EEG abnormalities consistent with cortical malformation
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with polymicrogyria (e.g., GPR56, TUBB2B)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: MRI confirmation of bilateral frontal polymicrogyria plus presence of seizures and developmental delay
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on neuroimaging combined with clinical features; genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

laboratory: Possible metabolic screening abnormalities in some cases
imaging: MRI showing irregular cortical ribbon with excessive small gyri predominantly in bilateral frontal lobes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as GPR56, TUBB2B, or other polymicrogyria-associated genes
other: EEG abnormalities consistent with epileptiform activity
Neurodevelopmental assessment indicating cognitive and motor delays

distinguishingFeatures: Focal rather than bilateral frontal involvement on MRI
Often localized epilepsy without global developmental delay
Smooth brain surface with absent or reduced gyri

redFlags: Onset of refractory seizures in infancy
references: Leventer RJ, Guerrini R, Dobyns WB. Malformations of cortical development and epilepsy. Dialogues Clin Neurosci. 2008;10(1):47-62.
Barkovich AJ, Guerrini R, Kuzniecky RI, Jackson GD, Dobyns WB. A developmental and genetic classification for malformations of cortical development: update 2012. Brain. 2012;135(Pt 5):1348-1369.
